verses.text: Send lambs for the ruler of the land, from Selah across the wilderness to the mountain of daughter Zion.
At the crossings of the Arnon, the daughters of Moab will be like birds that can't find their way, like a nest that's been scattered.
Give advice! Make a fair decision! Give us shade as dark as night in the middle of the day. Hide the outcasts. Don't hand over the people on the run.
Let my outcasts stay with you. Give Moab somewhere to hide from the destroyer. The one who squeezed people for money is finished. The destruction stops, and the oppressors are gone from the land.
A throne will stand firm in faithful love. Someone trustworthy will sit on it in David's tent, judging fairly, seeking justice, and quick to do what's right.
We've heard how proud Moab is, full of arrogance, pride, and rage. All that bragging comes to nothing.
So Moab will cry for Moab. Everybody will wail. You'll grieve over the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, crushed by what's happened.

The fields of Heshbon and the vines of Sibmah are drying up. The rulers of the nations broke down those prized branches that reached Jazer and trailed out into the wilderness. Their shoots spread far and even crossed the sea.
So I'll cry with Jazer over the vines of Sibmah. Heshbon and Elealeh, I'll drench you with my tears. The battle shout has come down on your summer fruit and your harvest.
Joy and laughter have been taken out of the fruitful fields. Nobody's singing or cheering in the vineyards. Nobody's pressing grapes into wine. I've stopped the shouting.
That's why my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and everything inside me aches for Kir Heres.
When Moab goes up to the high place and wears himself out, then comes to his sanctuary to pray, it won't get him anywhere.
That's the word the LORD spoke about Moab before.
Now the LORD says, “Within three years, counted as exactly as a hired worker counts a contract, all of Moab's glory and its great crowds will be brought to shame. The few who remain will be weak.”
